conflicts.about: Which component draws the address book's category tabs: the prototype's GOV.UK tabs markup against the Ministry of Justice sub navigation Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling names.

positions.says: The category tabs are MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the page, with the INS frontend adding the MoJ package.
The list page is built from GOV.UK button, tabs, table, pagination, select and input components plus custom pieces.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling wins: the tabs are MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the list on that tab, and the INS frontend adds @ministryofjustice/frontend at the animals frontend's major version (req-1123). The prototype still decides the tab names, order and default. Its claim is not overruled because it also records the GOV.UK button, table, pagination, select and input components that are built as drawn.

conflicts.about: Whether the address search's JavaScript behaviour (the search-only layout that hides the fields, type-ahead results, hide and reveal on a pick, the 'Selected' announcement and the 'Enter address manually' button) is built, against the rule that every page works without JavaScript.

positions.says: inc-072's search-only layout that reveals the fields (req-1214, req-1217's hide and reveal, req-1864) waits as one waiting-on-design increment, design question 10.
Every page works fully without JavaScript, and JavaScript may only enhance a page that already works.
Every search is a form with a button that submits it, and nothing a trader needs is shown only by script.
'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' open with only the search; the fields are hidden until an address is picked or manual entry is chosen.
An 'Enter address manually' button reveals the fields.
Typing shows matching addresses in a list as the user types.

conflicts.outcome: Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling wins. When the lookup lands, the address search is built in its no-JavaScript version: a form whose submit button searches on the server, with the fields visible (req-2043). The search-only layout, type-ahead, hide and reveal on a pick, the 'Selected' announcement, the 'Enter address manually' button and the errors that reveal hidden fields (req-1214, req-1216, req-2044, req-1864, req-1285) wait as one waiting-on-design increment for design question 10, also blocked on the lookup; design is asked whether the GOV.UK address pattern with the fields always visible will do. Nothing is overruled: design may still keep these behaviours.

conflicts.about: Whether the address book's add offers 'Transporter' and hands over to the add-a-transporter pages now, as Design Release 2.1 does, while transporter management is blocked.

Nothing is overruled: the transporter rows are kept for when the block lifts.

conflicts.about: Whether the plants frontend takes any part of templates: the afternoon ruling's same-increment plants rule across the whole backlog, or the templates ruling's animals-only template mode.

positions.says: Where a row changes a page or behaviour plants also has, the same increment changes plants, across the whole backlog.
The templates ruling covers the plants calls for the templates theme; this ruling does not restate them.
Template mode is animals only: plants pages get no template mode, because templates cover the animals sets.
The Templates navigation item is added to plants' navigation too, linking across to Manage templates.
The plants types are left out of template mode until plants has templates.

conflicts.outcome: The afternoon ruling ranks first and hands the templates theme's plants calls to the templates ruling, so its same-increment rule is applied as the templates ruling applies it: plants' navigation gains a Templates item linking across to the animals frontend's Manage templates, in the same increment as animals (req-965); plants has no templates of its own, no template mode and no plants type in template creation (req-2050). Nothing is overruled: every position still backs what is built. This agrees with plants' own ledger ruling d-038, which parks reuse-previous-consignment and does not adopt the templates pattern.

conflicts.about: Which checks a journey page applies in template mode: the notification's own, or looser ones.

positions.says: Template mode may apply different validation from the notification journey on the same pages.
The ruling does not say which validation differs, for example whether mandatory fields may be left blank in a template.
A template can be saved with only some sections answered.
No trace fills most template-mode pages, so their checks in template mode are not shown.

conflicts.outcome: Neither the ruling, which hedges, nor the design, which does not show a page's checks in template mode, settles it; the default below is built, with the checks chosen by the mode in one place so an answer changes them without touching the pages.
conflicts.question: In template mode, should a journey page keep the notification's required-answer checks on 'Save and continue', or may a template leave a required answer blank?
conflicts.default: Live animals and germinal products template pages keep the notification's checks: malformed answers are refused, 'Save and continue' needs the page's required answers, and 'Save and return to overview' saves without required checks as it does for a notification. What Design Release 2.1 already does differently for a template stands: no arrival date is asked, the template name is optional, and a template can be saved with sections unanswered. Plants has no template mode.

conflicts.about: Whether 'Use template' starts a notification by following a link (a GET), as the prototype does, or by a form post.

positions.says: Every state change is a form post.
GOV.UK components are the toolbox.
A real constraint the prototype cannot express, such as validation or cross-service behaviour, overrides the prototype.
Each template card's 'Use template' is a link to /templates/<id>/use.
Each card's 'Use template' is a link to /templates/<slug>/use.
A GET to /templates/<slug>/use starts a new draft prefilled from the template and redirects to the hub.
GET /templates/:templateId/use renders no page and redirects.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling ranks first, and a state-changing GET bypasses the real services' request forgery protection as c-188 found: using a template is a form post. On the template page 'Use template' is a primary submit button in a form and looks as designed; on each card it is a GOV.UK secondary button in a form, keeping the 'Use template' wording beside 'View template'. Following any templates link (Create new template, View template, a Change link) stores nothing; storing happens on a form post. The prototype's GET route is set aside; its claims that the card and page offer 'Use template' and that using it starts a prefilled draft still stand.

conflicts.about: Whether a submitted notification's card Amend starts the amendment straight away (today) or goes through the amend confirmation page.

positions.says: Plants' amend landing moves to its review page behind a confirmation page with no pop-up; plants' only Amend today is on its card.
The amend confirmation stays a separate page at today's route.
Keep the card's status-driven links; do not flatten them to Copy as new and View.
The card's Amend posts and starts the amendment straight away.

The card's Amend, which DR1's judgement keeps on the card with its wording and accessible name, becomes a link to that page instead of posting straight away, in live animals, germinal products and plants. Nothing is overruled: the DR1 judgement still keeps the action on the card, and today's claims are the evidence of what changes. req-1084's 'Amend ... posts' needs the cross-area pass to align with this.

conflicts.about: What the status strip calls an AMEND notification in plants: 'Amending', as plants shows today, or 'Amend'.

conflicts.outcome: The 9 October afternoon ruling outranks the plants frontend: the strip reads 'Amend' in every set, plants included, through the same shared strip change as the Amend bar, with no plants-specific work (req-2061). repo-plantsfrontend-p1-030 is not overruled: it records today's strip, which req-2061 cites as what changes, and the rest of it (the yellow tag on an amendment) still holds. The list card's 'Amending' tag is not named by the ruling and stays as the list area has it.

conflicts.about: Whether plants' 'Save and return to overview' refuses a page for a missing required answer

positions.says: inc-003 also changes plants: its pages with exit=hub save without required checks, but malformed answers are still refused.

conflicts.about: Which answers a template holds: every answer a notification holds, as the templates ruling's hedged 'maybe the same data' reads, or only those Design Release 2.1 saves, which leave out the arrival date and the transit countries.

positions.says: Template mode captures the same data as the notification journey (Sam hedges with 'maybe').
The prototype decides look and feel, including which questions are asked of which goods.
A Design Release 2.1 template never saves an arrival date.
The template page's Change links include transit countries.
The template page's Arrival details card holds no arrival date or time.

conflicts.outcome: The templates ruling hedges, and its own claims 34 and 35 leave the differences between template mode and a notification open; the 9 October ruling gives the prototype which questions are asked; and Design Release 2.1 contradicts itself on transit countries (a Change link for answers it never saves). Neither precedence nor a ruling settles it, so the default below is built.
conflicts.question: Does a template hold every answer a notification holds, including the arrival date and transit countries, or only the answers Design Release 2.1 saves?
conflicts.default: In both animals sets a template stores its answers in the notification's own shape on the same pages, with no separate template data model. It never asks for or holds the arrival date or time (req-1345) or documents (req-1334), as Design Release 2.1 shows. A live animals template holds the transit countries as answered and seeds them, because the design's template page offers their Change link (req-2112). A germinal products template holds whatever the germinal set's pages ask, less the arrival date. Plants has no templates.
